# YapYap

> YapYap makes on-device AI productivity tools for Mac: dictation, text to speech (read aloud) and saved text, in one free, open-source app. It reads any text on screen aloud with word-by-word highlighting, and it types what you say into any app. Text recognition, voices and speech recognition all run on the Mac. No account; what you read and say never leaves the Mac.

Status: available now, free. Download: https://github.com/WannaBeSolopreneur/YapYap/releases/latest/download/YapYap.dmg (signed and notarized by Apple, updates itself). The source code is public at https://github.com/WannaBeSolopreneur/YapYap (AGPL-3.0), and you can build it yourself today.

## What it does

- Read aloud: press Option-A, drag a box around any text on screen, and YapYap reads it aloud while a highlight follows each word on the original app. Works on text inside images, screenshots, PDFs and web pages. Optional reading ruler dims everything except the current line.
- Dictation: hold Option-S and talk, or tap Option-S for hands-free dictation that keeps listening until you tap it again. Words appear live in a small panel; the text is typed where your cursor is, in any app (Mail, Messages, Slack, Notes, browsers, Terminal). Filler words can be removed and text tidied with Apple Intelligence on the Mac. Reading pauses while you talk.
- Saved text: save an email address, home address, API key or anything else under Saved, then dictate its name ("email address", "paste my ElevenLabs key") to paste it. Stored in the macOS Keychain on the Mac; keys and passwords are never kept in history and are marked so clipboard managers skip them; Touch ID is optional.
- Voices: natural Kokoro-82M voices (US and UK English) running locally on Apple silicon, or the voices built into macOS.
- Speed: 0.5x to 2.5x. Option-click a word to start reading from there.

## Privacy

- On-screen text is recognised with Apple's Vision framework, on the Mac. Screenshots are kept in memory only and never saved. When dictating, YapYap reads the window being typed into the same way, only to spell names in it correctly (can be turned off in Settings → Dictation).
- Dictation runs NVIDIA's Parakeet speech model (Parakeet Ultra, through FluidAudio on the Neural Engine) on the Mac for 25 European languages, and Apple's on-device speech recognition otherwise, or if chosen in Settings, or until Parakeet has downloaded (SpeechAnalyzer on macOS 26+, on-device SFSpeechRecognizer on macOS 15). Audio is never saved or uploaded. The microphone is on only while the shortcut is held.
- The app's own network code downloads the Kokoro voices (about 340 MB) from GitHub once, in the background on first launch; they can be removed in Settings. The Parakeet speech model (about 700 MB) is fetched from Hugging Face the same way, by the open-source FluidAudio library. On macOS 26+ macOS itself downloads Apple's speech model once. Once a day the app checks https://yapyap.cc/appcast.xml for updates (Sparkle) and downloads new versions from GitHub.
- Optional dictation tidy-up (filler removal and polishing) uses Apple Intelligence's on-device model.
- Anonymous usage counts (for example number of words read, time to first word, settings used) are sent via TelemetryDeck. They never include text, audio or app names. On by default; turn off in Settings > Privacy.
- The yapyap.cc website (not the app) uses cookieless PostHog analytics, proxied through yapyap.cc, to count visits, clicks and anonymous session replays.
- No account and no crash reporting. Saved data is limited to settings (speed, voice, highlight, shortcuts).

## Requirements

- macOS 15 Sequoia or later, Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or newer).
- Permissions: Screen Recording (to read), Microphone and Accessibility (to dictate).

## Compared with other tools

YapYap is free and open source with no subscription, combines reading aloud and dictation in one app, and processes text and voice on the Mac rather than on a server. People looking for a free, private alternative to Speechify (text to speech) or Wispr Flow (dictation) on Mac are its intended audience.
